method: Short, attributed snippets from named ATMAP/TCMA transliterations (CC BY-SA 3.0), not a locally mirrored edition. Editorial glosses and interpretations are independently written summaries, not certified translations. Missing signs, damaged signs and queried readings are preserved. Museum catalogue-only objects show no invented text. Expert collation remains outstanding.

items.edition_credit: Jacob Jan de Ridder, ATMAP/TCMA edition of KAJ 247 (2020), CC BY-SA 3.0
items.editorial_scope: Workers, temple setting and restored eponym marker
items.status_note: The edition labels the document Receipt? and questions the worker designation. A restored eponym marker does not mean every sign physically survives.

lines.gloss: The editor reads twenty-two people in a questioned labour category; the damaged-sign marks must be retained.
lines.interpretation: The person category is interpreted cautiously; this is not a census of the city.
lines.note: The corner marks indicate damaged but partially visible signs. The edition adds a question mark to the worker interpretation.

lines.gloss: A reference to an institutional temple setting in the published passage.
lines.interpretation: A temple location does not establish what each named person believed or did.
lines.note: Logographic notation is retained from the line; the English statement is an editorial contextual cue.

lines.gloss: The eponym marker is reconstructed in the modern edition.
lines.interpretation: Square brackets mean the corresponding signs are supplied rather than intact.
lines.note: This explicitly illustrates restoration, not a surviving undamaged written word.

items.edition_credit: Jacob Jan de Ridder, ATMAP/TCMA edition of MARV 10, 07 (2020), CC BY-SA 3.0
items.editorial_scope: Named recipient and uncertain campaign phrase
items.status_note: The campaign reading contains explicit damage and editorial uncertainty; no definite journey is reconstructed.

lines.gloss: The entry introduces a recipient named Niri-šaldi, according to the published edition.
lines.interpretation: The next lines supply a legal-status designation; one receipt is not a complete biography.
lines.note: The upper corner brackets delimit damaged but readable parts of the personal name.

lines.gloss: The edition queries the wording used to connect the issue with a journey or campaign.
lines.interpretation: A proposed expedition context is not a verified travel route.
lines.note: Damage brackets and editor marks including ! and ? are deliberately preserved.

items.edition_credit: Jacob Jan de Ridder, ATMAP/TCMA edition of KAJ 233 / KAV 207 (2020), CC BY-SA 3.0
items.editorial_scope: Barley measure and dated eponym formula
items.status_note: Ancient units are not converted to litres or modern rations without a metrological study.

lines.gloss: This sequence records a barley measure using original numerals and capacity signs.
lines.interpretation: The editor links the allocation to a service horse in the following lines; it is not a general cavalry ration rule.
lines.note: The sign sequence is a short extract, not a normalized Akkadian sentence.

lines.gloss: The dating formula includes the month Kuzallu and a thirteenth day.
lines.interpretation: The following line gives an eponym, but a precise absolute BCE date is not independently established here.
lines.note: Calendar and eponym are not automatically equivalent to a modern calendar year.

items.edition_credit: Jacob Jan de Ridder, ATMAP/TCMA edition of MARV 1, 12 / VS 19, 12 (2020), CC BY-SA 3.0
items.status_note: Individual group totals and institutional distribution are documented in the linked edition, not transcribed in full here.

lines.gloss: The opening records barley quantity in Assyrian scribal measures.
lines.interpretation: The following lines classify the provisioned guard groups; the opening figure alone cannot establish individual diet.
lines.note: The group descriptions on the obverse and reverse must be consulted with the original edition.

lines.gloss: The source links the provisioned allotment to ten days.
lines.interpretation: A ten-day record cannot be generalized into a year-round ration or proof of food actually eaten.
lines.note: The translated sense belongs to the editor's connected passage, not an independent philological collation.

items.edition_credit: Jacob Jan de Ridder, ATMAP/TCMA edition of KAJ 144 (2020), CC BY-SA 3.0
items.editorial_scope: Lead measures and house transaction wording
items.status_note: This tablet's subgenre is marked Receipt?; the line does not establish all terms of the house sale.

lines.gloss: The text opens its legal-economic statement with a lead quantity in talents and minas.
lines.interpretation: The associated house transaction appears over connected lines, so the amount alone is not a modern property valuation.
lines.note: Ancient measures are retained, and no exchange rate or modern currency value is asserted.

lines.gloss: The clause relates the sum to a house sale in the edition's reading.
lines.interpretation: This does not establish the ultimate outcome or occupancy of the property.
lines.note: The partially damaged na sign is preserved with its original editorial marks.

items.edition_credit: Jacob Jan de Ridder, ATMAP/TCMA edition of Billa 30 (2020), CC BY-SA 3.0
items.editorial_scope: Provincial barley entry, questioned obligation and broken names
items.status_note: The account is a receipt; an obligation verb is queried and the witnesses and some date signs are broken.

lines.gloss: The editor records a barley amount and an additional payment phrase.
lines.interpretation: Its economic nature is apparent, while the precise imposition on people remains qualified.
lines.note: The compact excerpt retains ancient measure signs rather than a modern unit conversion.

lines.gloss: An editorial question mark qualifies the word describing the imposition or obligation.
lines.interpretation: The precise legal nature of the demand cannot be stated as certain.
lines.note: A queried sign or reading is evidence of uncertainty in the modern edition.

lines.gloss: The line preserves lost or unreadable portions of a personal name.
lines.interpretation: A missing name must not be reconstructed into an invented individual.
lines.note: Brackets and x indicate missing or unidentified signs. This example is not a readable full name.

items.edition_credit: Jacob Jan de Ridder, ATMAP/TCMA edition of KAJ 118 (2020), CC BY-SA 3.0
items.editorial_scope: Palace straw and a broken reverse
items.status_note: The initial quantity is readable; later reverse lines have major losses and cannot establish every participant.

lines.gloss: The opening gives forty sacks associated with straw in the published edition.
lines.interpretation: Other lines describe institutional custody; this alone is not evidence of a regional harvest.
lines.note: Commodity and count are a specific account, not a universal agrarian rate.

lines.gloss: The edition has gaps where groups of signs are missing.
lines.interpretation: The reverse cannot be silently filled in with reconstructed names or actions.
lines.note: The ellipses denote lost signs; they are not the author's punctuation replacing a known reading.

items.edition_credit: Metropolitan Museum of Art, object catalogue 62.85.3; no published line edition confirmed
items.editorial_scope: Object has two seal impressions; no individual sign or transliteration confirmed
items.status_note: The museum object page identifies the physical tablet, but no trustworthy line-by-line transcription or translation was verified for this release. No cuneiform text is reconstructed.

items.edition_credit: British Museum BM 21901, Babylonian Chronicle catalogue; a line-specific edition comparison remains pending
items.editorial_scope: Chronicle records the fall of Nineveh; no verbatim line collation supplied here
items.status_note: The tablet is a later copy of earlier historical events. The catalogue is useful provenance evidence; exact Akkadian lines and published translation variants require specialist edition collation before display.
